questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: Under the Cloud Shared Responsibility Model for IaaS compute (e.g., AWS EC2), who patches the guest operating system and runtime libraries?

options.text: Virtual machines never need OS patches in the cloud
The customer
The cloud provider exclusively
The DNS registrar

questions.explanation: The provider secures physical hardware, facilities, and hypervisor ('Security OF the Cloud'); the customer secures guest OS, IAM, network rules, and data ('Security IN the Cloud').

questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: Which cloud service model manages OS, runtime scaling, and patching automatically so developers focus strictly on application code and data?

options.text: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
Bare-metal colocation
Client-side local hosting

questions.explanation: PaaS abstracts underlying servers and operating systems, while IaaS exposes raw virtualized compute and networking control.

questions.prompt: What is an Availability Zone (AZ) within a cloud provider Region?

options.text: An entire continental geography
A single browser CDN edge cache
An internal IAM group policy
One or more discrete physical data centers with independent power, cooling, and low-latency fiber inside a Region

options.text: Relational OLTP SQL row lock table
In-memory Redis key-value store
Object storage (e.g., Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage)
Local instance ephemeral NVMe scratch disk

questions.prompt: Which capabilities define a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)?

options.text: Automatic public exposure of all internal databases to 0.0.0.0/0
Custom IPv4/IPv6 CIDR address range segmentation across public and private subnets
Explicit route tables controlling Internet Gateway and NAT Gateway traffic
Stateful Security Groups and stateless Network ACL perimeter filtering

questions.prompt: What is the security principle of Least Privilege in cloud IAM?

options.text: Granting identities only the exact actions and resources needed for their task and nothing more
Assigning AdministratorAccess globally to reduce permission tickets
Sharing one root account key pair across engineers
Turning off MFA on service roles

questions.prompt: In cloud networking, why do application tiers placed in private subnets use a NAT Gateway?

options.text: To bypass all IAM authentication tokens
To run relational SQL joins in hardware
To assign public static IPv4 addresses directly to database instances
To initiate outbound internet updates/API requests without allowing unsolicited inbound internet connections

questions.explanation: NAT Gateways allow private instances to pull security patches or talk to external webhooks safely without inbound public exposure.

Complete elimination of network latency between continents
Reproducible, version-controlled environment provisioning via Git pull requests
Automated drift detection against desired declared cloud state

questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: What happens when an Explicit Deny statement and an Allow statement both match an IAM action?

options.text: The most recently created JSON line wins arbitrarily
An Explicit Deny always overrides any Allow rule
Allow overrides Deny if attached directly to a user
The request enters a 5-second approval hold

questions.explanation: Cloud IAM evaluation denies by default, allows if explicitly allowed with no deny, and ALWAYS denies whenever any explicit Deny matches.

questions.prompt: Which pricing model typically offers the steepest discount (up to ~70-90%) for fault-tolerant, stateless batch workloads that can handle 2-minute interruption notices?

options.text: Spot / Preemptible Instances
On-Demand Instances
Dedicated Physical Hosts
Unreserved Static NAT Gateways

questions.explanation: Spot instances consume spare provider capacity at deep discounts for interruptible or checkpointed batch tasks.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: Identify why a microservice EC2 instance fails to read a secret key from `s3://corp-secrets-prod/config.json` despite having `AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess` via Security Group:

options.text: JSON files cannot be stored in S3 buckets
Security Groups control network ports/IPs (not S3 IAM API authorization); the instance needs an IAM Instance Profile Role granting `s3:GetObject`
S3 requires port 22 SSH access enabled in Security Groups
EC2 instances cannot communicate with S3 over HTTPS

questions.explanation: Never confuse VPC network firewalling (Security Groups) with IAM service authorization policies (Roles attached to compute).
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: Look at this VPC subnet CIDR: `10.0.1.0/26`. A deployment script fails to spin up a 70-node Kubernetes cluster inside it. Why?

options.text: A `/26` subnet contains only 64 total IPs (and ~59-62 usable hosts after reserved cloud IPs), insufficient for 70 nodes
10.0.0.0/8 addresses are not private RFC 1918 ranges
Kubernetes only supports IPv6 CIDRs
Subnet `/26` masks give 4,096 addresses

questions.explanation: A `/26` yields 2^(32-26) = 64 IPs (cloud providers reserve 5 IPs in each subnet -> 59 usable), so at least a `/25` (128 IPs) or `/24` is needed.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: A web server inside a public subnet responds to HTTP requests on port 80, yet times out when the Security Group outbound rules were stripped to empty, while inbound 80 was open. If it uses a stateless NACL with NO outbound rule for ephemeral ports (1024-65535), what occurs?

options.text: NACL rules are stateful like Security Groups
HTTP requests return on port 21 FTP
Ephemeral ports range from 1 to 100 only
Stateless NACLs block return HTTP response packets targeting client ephemeral ports unless explicitly permitted outbound

questions.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless and evaluate inbound AND outbound rules separately, whereas Security Groups are stateful and allow return traffic automatically.
questions.topic: Stateful Security Groups vs Stateless NACLs
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: An AWS Lambda function inside a VPC subnet has fast local DB calls but hangs when calling an external Stripe payment API. What is the root cause?

options.text: Stripe requires running instances on bare-metal hardware
IAM roles prevent all HTTPS DNS resolution
Lambda inside private subnets has no default public IP and requires a NAT Gateway (or route to internet) for external outbound endpoints
Lambda cannot run HTTPS calls in Node.js

questions.explanation: VPC-attached Lambda functions never receive public IPs; internet egress must traverse a private subnet route -> NAT Gateway -> Internet Gateway.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: Review this IAM policy snippet attached to a CI deployment user. Why does it violate Least Privilege?

options.text: CI pipelines require root privileges by specification
Wildcard `Action: '*'` and `Resource: '*'` grants full unrestricted admin across all cloud services and accounts
JSON keys must be lowercase
`Effect` must always be `'Permit'`

questions.explanation: Scoped policies specify exact needed actions (`s3:PutObject`, `ecs:UpdateService`) and exact ARN resources.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: You want an S3 bucket hosting frontend assets to deliver globally under 50ms latency while blocking direct raw S3 URL access. How do you configure this?

options.text: Serve assets synchronously from a relational Postgres BYTEA table
Keep S3 completely private (`BlockPublicAccess`), put CloudFront CDN in front, and authorize only CloudFront via Origin Access Control (OAC)
Set ACL `public-read-write` on the S3 bucket globally
Deploy 50 EC2 instances copying files via rsync

questions.explanation: CloudFront + OAC keeps the origin bucket locked private while caching assets across global edge POPs.

questions.prompt: A multi-AZ stateless microservice fails health checks intermittently during rolling deployments causing HTTP 502 spikes. How do you eliminate dropped in-flight requests?

options.text: Enable Load Balancer connection draining (deregistration delay) and handle SIGTERM gracefully before closing the HTTP listener
Reduce health check interval to 100ms with threshold 1
Disable HTTPS TLS termination on the load balancer
Hardkill containers with SIGKILL immediately on scaling down

questions.explanation: Connection draining allows active requests to complete while stopping new traffic to terminating pods.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: An engineering team committed long-lived IAM Access Keys into GitHub by mistake. Besides rotating/revoking those keys, how do you permanently prevent key leaks in GitHub Actions deployments?

options.text: Rename variables from `AWS_SECRET` to `CONFIG_KEY_1`
Commit keys encoded in Base64 into `.github/keys.txt`
Assign MFA hardware keys via email attachments
Use OpenID Connect (OIDC) federation so GitHub Actions assumes short-lived temporary IAM roles without storing static secret keys

questions.explanation: OIDC federation mints short-lived STS tokens scoped to the repository/branch claim, eliminating static secret keys entirely.

questions.prompt: How do you achieve automatic horizontal resilience for an Auto Scaling Group if a full Availability Zone becomes unavailable?

options.text: Save user sessions on each EC2 instance local `/tmp` disk
Disable Auto Scaling health checks so crashed instances stay registered
Spread subnets across at least 2–3 Availability Zones, use Elastic Load Balancing across them, and externalize session state into Redis/RDS
Place all instances in a single larger subnet in AZ-1a

questions.explanation: Stateless compute across multiple AZs behind a load balancer ensures regional continuity when one AZ goes down.

questions.prompt: A data warehouse exports terabytes monthly across cloud regions, inflating NAT Gateway and cross-region egress fees. What reduces network cost without breaking private access to S3?

options.text: Turn off TLS encryption on transfers
Configure a VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 so traffic stays inside the private cloud backbone bypassing NAT Gateway data charges
Route S3 traffic over the public internet using Elastic IPs
Spin up two extra NAT Gateways per subnet

questions.explanation: S3 Gateway VPC Endpoints are free and route bucket transfers directly within the VPC without per-GB NAT Gateway processing fees.

questions.prompt: Which Terraform block best enforces remote locking so two engineers executing `terraform apply` simultaneously cannot corrupt state?

options.text: Disable state files entirely with `-state=none`
Configure an S3 remote backend with state locking (`use_lockfile = true` / DynamoDB lock table) and versioning enabled
Commit `terraform.tfstate` directly to Git main branch
Pass `--auto-approve` to override concurrent runs

questions.explanation: Remote encrypted backends with lock coordination guarantee atomic single-writer applies across team pipelines.

questions.prompt: Which IAM Resource Policy condition guarantees bucket objects can only be downloaded over encrypted HTTPS (TLS) connections?

options.text: "Bool": { "aws:SecureTransport": "false" }
"StringEquals": { "aws:Protocol": "HTTP" }
"Bool": { "aws:PublicAccess": "true" }
"NumericLessThan": { "aws:Port": 80 }

questions.explanation: Explicitly denying requests when `aws:SecureTransport` is false enforces TLS in transit for all bucket operations.

questions.prompt: To make a container image small, fast to push, and minimal attack surface, which Dockerfile practice should you apply?

options.text: Bundle build compilers, test fixtures, and `.git` history in the final Ubuntu image
Run container entrypoints as root (UID 0) without a healthcheck
Hardcode `.env` production secrets inside `ENV` statements
Use multi-stage builds compiling in an SDK image and copying only runtime binaries into a minimal distroless/alpine runtime image

questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds discard compilers and source artifacts, yielding lean runtime images with minimal CVE exposure.

questions.prompt: You need an S3 Lifecycle rule to retain compliance audit logs for 7 years while minimizing storage expenses after 90 days. What transition rule applies?

options.text: Copy objects onto gp3 EBS SSD volumes attached to stopped VMs
Download objects locally to laptop storage monthly
Transition objects to Standard-IA at 30 days and Glacier Deep Archive at 90 days, expiring after 2555 days
Replicate objects across 12 Standard S3 buckets globally forever

questions.explanation: Automated lifecycle rules tier infrequent logs down to cold archive classes at pennies per TB-month.

questions.prompt: When designing a Kubernetes Readiness vs Liveness probe, what happens differently when a Readiness probe fails?

options.text: Liveness never restarts crashed processes
Kubernetes removes the Pod IP from Service load balancing endpoints without restarting the container; Liveness failure triggers container restart
Both Readiness and Liveness delete the underlying PersistentVolume
Readiness failures terminate the entire worker node immediately

questions.explanation: Readiness stops routing traffic while a pod warms up or recovers temporarily; Liveness restarts deadlocked containers.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: A mission-critical payment API requires Recovery Time Objective (RTO) < 5 minutes and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) < 1 minute across geographic regions. Which DR strategy meets both targets?

options.text: Manual infrastructure rebuild from wiki documentation during an outage
Multi-region Active-Active or Warm Standby topology with continuous cross-region database replication and Route 53 latency/health failover
Daily nightly cold snapshots uploaded to manual tape archives
Single-AZ RDS instance with weekly backups

questions.explanation: RTO < 5m and RPO < 1m eliminate cold Backup-and-Restore options, demanding continuously replicated standby or active-active regional clusters.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in Cloud Computing

questions.prompt: Following the 12-Factor App methodology, how should configuration secrets (API keys, DB URLs) reach cloud containers across Dev, Staging, and Production?

options.text: Inject environment configuration cleanly at runtime via a managed Secrets Manager / Vault rather than committing files inside the container image
Build three separate Dockerfiles containing hardcoded staging/prod secrets
Read secrets from a public GitHub Gist during startup
Prompt the operator via stdin on container boot

questions.explanation: Keeping the exact same immutable build artifact across all environments while injecting runtime config via Secrets Manager prevents leaks.

questions.prompt: An organization spans 40 cloud accounts across Dev, QA, and Production workloads. How should security teams enforce mandatory guardrails (like blocking disabling CloudTrail or unencrypted S3) organization-wide?

options.text: Send Slack reminders asking engineers not to click dangerous buttons
Manually review bills once per quarter
Grant every team a shared single root login to audit each other
Apply Service Control Policies (SCPs) at the AWS Organizations / Management Group root restricting prohibited actions even for account admins

questions.explanation: Organization-wide SCP guardrails define maximum permission boundaries across all member accounts simultaneously.
